subject.title: Feature: browser tool - expose CDP Network domain for request interception

question: Should OpenClaw expose a model-facing browser network inspection/interception API, and if so should the first supported shape be passive inspection only or active request interception/mutation?
rationale: The issue is valid but changes the browser tool contract and sensitive-data boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent policy or API shape without maintainer intent.

options.title: Ship passive inspection first
options.body: Expose a gated model-facing request list and bounded response-body action with redaction and profile capability rules, while deferring active interception.

options.title: Design full interception
options.body: Approve a broader CDP Network interception/mutation contract, but require an explicit permissions, redaction, and profile-support design before implementation.

options.title: Keep it operator-only
options.body: Decline model-facing exposure for now and leave network diagnostics to CLI/control-server debugging commands.

recommendation.title: Ship passive inspection first
recommendation.body: Expose a gated model-facing request list and bounded response-body action with redaction and profile capability rules, while deferring active interception.

likelyOwner.reason: The browser plugin schema, dispatcher, and runtime ownership history point to steipete as the strongest routing candidate for the product/security call.
